messages.text: Wednesday, November 18 · Canton, Michigan
Bronze bells, ancient ice, and a quiet shift toward winter

The day brings overcast skies and mild temperatures as we settle into the late autumn rhythm. Local focus turns to the resonance of historical instruments and the long-range implications of distant planetary science.
Expect overcast conditions today with a high near 57 degrees and a low around 27 degrees.
The sun rises at 7:28 AM and sets at 5:09 PM, with the moon in its first-quarter phase at 57.6 percent illumination.
Midday music and afternoon inquiry
Tiffany Ng performs a carillon recital on the 53 bronze bells of Burton Memorial Tower at 12:00 PM. Later, the East Hall hosts a seminar on algebraic combinatorics at 2:30 PM.
The 862 Meeting is scheduled for this evening at 6:30 PM.
Faculty senate and local governance

The University of Michigan Faculty Senate recently passed a vote of no confidence regarding university leadership and police department negotiations. This follows broader regional shifts in political control that continue to influence policy discussions across the state.
Looking toward the weekend
The Girls Gear Up outreach event is set for the morning of November 21 at 7:30 AM.

Thursday, November 19 · Canton, Michigan
Carillon bells, improv stages, and the quiet shift of autumn light
An overcast Wednesday brings mild temperatures and a steady rhythm of local performances. We look at the intersection of community storytelling and recent shifts in public health status.
Expect an overcast day with a high near 64 degrees and a low around 33 degrees.
The sun rises at 7:30 AM and sets at 5:09 PM, with the moon currently in its first-quarter phase at 67.3% illumination.
Midweek resonance and local stages

Lon Mitchell performs a carillon recital at the Lurie Ann and Robert H. Tower in Ann Arbor at 1:20 PM. Later, catch the storytelling and improv show For Real at Go Comedy Improv Theater in Ferndale at 7:30 PM.
The Girls Gear Up outreach event is scheduled for the morning of November 21.
University policy and public health concerns

The University of Michigan Faculty Senate recently passed a vote of no confidence regarding the administration's handling of police and labor negotiations. Separately, experts continue to advise on the health risks associated with kratom products as local restrictions emerge.
